logline: A teenage boy in a Norwegian industrial town discovers he may be the reincarnation of Thor, and that the factory-owning family who controls the town are ancient giants slowly poisoning the environment.

renewal.note: Three-season run concluded with Season 3 in August 2023. The series finale revealed the entire conflict may have existed within the protagonist's imagination, a narrative choice that divided audiences sharply.

bollymeter.basis: A 70% Rotten Tomatoes score from 10 critics reflected divided reception: the show's intimate scale and environmental allegory were praised, but several critics found the pacing too modest for its mythological ambitions.

pull_quotes.text: Its intimate scale grounds Norse folklore in an approachable way that ought to appeal to young adult viewers.

seasons.review_body: Ragnarok launched on Netflix in January 2020, refracting Norse mythology through a contemporary Norwegian town threatened by industrial pollution. The series leans into an environmental allegory and opts to keep the scale intimate rather than spectacle-driven, creating a slow burn that grounds the myth in teen drama. It treats the mythological weight with restraint, which can make the pacing feel like a mismatch for viewers expecting a bigger ramp-up. The production values are notably pretty, even as the overall tone lands closer to a tepid teen drama.

episode_reviews.title: New Boy
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere establishes the fictional town of Edda as a place where environmental rot and economic power are the same thing, and introduces Magne as an unremarkable teenager about to become something else. The Jutul family's introductory scene is the season's most unsettling five minutes.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Magne catches a hammer thrown at him without flinching - the first signal that something mythological is stirring beneath the mundane surface.

bollymeter.basis: An 84% Rotten Tomatoes score from a single review limits inference, but audience scores held and the season expanded the mythology with more characters embodying Norse deities.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 arrived in May 2021 and expanded the cast of mythologically awakened characters, introducing other figures from the Norse pantheon into Magne's conflict with the Jotun family. The season deepened the environmental stakes and gave the show's central allegory more narrative room, with the industrial pollution plot becoming explicitly political. The single Rotten Tomatoes critic review posted an 84% score; the small sample prevents confident extrapolation. Audience reception was stable, suggesting the season held its core viewership without dramatically expanding it. The show's fundamental tension between YA drama conventions and mythological ambition remained productive if unresolved.
seasons.season_over_season: Season 2 broadens the Norse mythology cast and clarifies the environmental allegory; pacing improved modestly though the scale remained deliberately contained.

bollymeter.basis: A 24% Rotten Tomatoes score and severely negative audience reception tracked a finale that revealed the entire conflict may have existed within the protagonist's imagination - a narrative choice that divided the show's audience sharply and the finale episode rated 3.6 on IMDb.

seasons.review_body: Season 3 released in August 2023 and the streaming finale controversy became a major talking point that year. The narrative revealed that the entire Norse mythology conflict may have existed within Magne's imagination, framed as his response to grief and based on a comic book he created. The ending effectively invalidated the preceding two seasons for a large portion of the audience. The Rotten Tomatoes score fell to 24% and the finale episode was rated 3.6 on IMDb, among the lowest scores for any episode of a Netflix series. The only available critic review said the finale approach served as a reminder that fidelity to myth would have benefited the show more than its comic book interpretation.
seasons.season_over_season: A catastrophic drop from Season 2: the ambiguous-reality finale alienated the established audience and drew near-universal viewer rejection on review platforms.
